subtitle: The General Who Ruled from Behind the Lion Throne

panels.shot: dramatic split-panel composition, one half in courtly gold, the other in storm-dark battlefield hues
panels.action: On one side Krishnaraja Wodeyar II sits on an ornate lion throne in full ceremonial splendor; on the other, Hyder Ali stands in battle armor amid cannon and rocket troops, their figures overlapping in the center like one long shadow.

dialogue.text: In Mysore, the lion throne still shone under Krishnaraja Wodeyar II, but by 1761 another hand—Hyder Ali’s—quietly tightened on the real reins of power.

i18n.hi: मैसूर में कृष्णराज वोडेयार द्वितीय के नीचे शेर सिंहासन चमकता रहा, मगर 1761 तक असली लगाम चुपचाप हायदर अली के हाथ में आ चुकी थी।

panels.shot: wide aerial view of the Deccan, map-like, with armies and banners moving like currents
panels.action: The subcontinent stretches below like a living map, Maratha horsemen sweeping one way, the Nizam’s lines another, French and Company camps on the coasts, while a smaller yet fierce Mysore force marches from its hill country.

dialogue.text: The mid-eighteenth century Deccan was a chessboard of restless powers—Marathas, the Nizam, French adventurers, and the rising English Company—all jostling for forts, tribute and fragile allies.

i18n.hi: अठारहवीं सदी के मध्य का दक्खन मानो शतरंज की बिसात था—मराठे, निज़ाम, फ़्रांसीसी मु冒िं और उभरती इंग्लिश कंपनी क़िले, नज़राने और नाज़ुक दोस्तियों के लिए टकरा रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Krishnaraja Wodeyar II in court, slightly elevated angle showing isolation amid grandeur
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar II sits young and slender on the lion throne in Srirangapatna’s durbar hall, gilded pillars and silk courtiers around him, yet his face is pensive as rival factions whisper in the shadows.

dialogue.text: In Srirangapatna the Wodeyar king, Krishnaraja II, wore jewels and titles, but his court was split by ministers and generals who fought over revenues, forts and commands.

i18n.hi: श्रीरंगपटना में वोडेयार राजा कृष्णराज द्वितीय तो गहने और ख़िताब पहने थे, पर दरबार मंत्रियों और फ़ौजी सरदारों की खींचतान से दो फाड़ था—आमदनी, क़िलों और फौजी हुक्मों पर झगड़े उबल रहे थे।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Hyder Ali in a campaign tent over maps, lamplight flickering
panels.action: Hyder Ali, broad-shouldered and intense, leans over a rough campaign table strewn with maps and gun-metal instruments, a simple turban on his head as he traces routes with a calloused finger.

dialogue.text: Into this confusion rose Hyder Ali, once a modest officer, who built his name not in poetry or pedigree, but in marches, sieges and the hard science of war.

i18n.hi: इसी अफ़रा-तफ़री से उठा हायदर अली—एक मामूली अफ़सर से—जिसने नाम न तो शेरो-शायरी से कमाया, न वंश से, बल्कि कूचों, घेराबंदियों और जंग के सख़्त हुनर से।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide shot, slightly low angle, showing infantry lines and artillery
panels.action: On a dusty plain Mysore infantry stand in disciplined ranks beside field guns, smoke curling from their barrels, as Hyder Ali rides along the line on a sturdy horse, hand raised in firm command.

dialogue.text: He drilled infantry in steady lines, matched cannon with cannon, and in his train marched something new for the region—organized rocket troops, shrieking fire arcing over enemy ranks.

i18n.hi: उसने पैदल फौज को सीधी कतारों में साधा, तोप का जवाब तोप से दिया, और उसके साथ चली एक नई चीज़—संगठित रॉकेट दस्ता, जो चीखती आग बनकर दुश्मन की कतारों पर झूलती थी।

panels.shot: close-up on a steel rocket tube being prepared, hands working with precision
panels.action: Mysore soldiers kneel as they fix metal rockets to bamboo shafts, binding them carefully, a distant Hyder Ali watching with a calculating gaze, while a stormy sky looms above.

dialogue.text: These iron-cased rockets were crude by later standards, yet in the smoky confusion of eighteenth-century battles they terrified cavalry and broke proud charges into stumbling retreats.

i18n.hi: ये लोहे के खोके वाले रॉकेट बाद के ज़माने से भले ही भोंडे थे, मगर धुएँ से भरी अठारहवीं सदी की जंगों में घुड़सवारों के दिल दहला देते, और शान से दौड़ती टुकड़ियों को लड़खड़ाती वापसी में बदल देते।

panels.shot: interior durbar medium-wide, with Hyder in plain soldier’s garb amid richly dressed nobles
panels.action: In the durbar hall, silk-clad nobles sit cross-legged, some frowning, as Hyder Ali stands at the edge in plain but neat soldier’s dress, scrolls of revenue accounts in his hand instead of weapons.

dialogue.text: But Hyder Ali did not stop at the field. He moved into accounts, garrisons and grain, building loyalty in camps and treasuries while old courtiers traded insults and petitions.

i18n.hi: पर हायदर अली ने मैदान तक बात नहीं रोकी। वह हिसाब-किताब, क़िलों की चौकियों और अन्न-गोड़ामों तक उतरा, कैंप और ख़ज़ानों में वफ़ादारी खड़ी करता रहा, जबकि पुराने दरबारी गालियाँ और अर्ज़ियाँ बाँटते रह गए।

panels.shot: two-shot, side view, of Hyder and Krishnaraja walking in a palace corridor, light and shadow
panels.action: In a long colonnaded corridor, Krishnaraja Wodeyar II walks in fine garments while Hyder Ali, slightly behind and to the side, gestures respectfully; shafts of light from one side leave the king shining while Hyder’s figure falls partly in shadow.

dialogue.speaker: Krishnaraja Wodeyar II
dialogue.text: If you guard my kingdom, Hyder, the throne will honor your service.

i18n.hi: “अगर तुम मेरी रियासत की हिफ़ाज़त करो, हायदर, तो सिंहासन तुम्हारी ख़िदमत का मान रखेगा।”

panels.shot: medium shot from behind the throne, showing Hyder standing at its rear, courtiers arrayed ahead
panels.action: The camera looks from behind the lion throne; Krishnaraja Wodeyar II sits facing the court, while just behind the throne’s back Hyder Ali stands, arms folded, watching rows of nobles and officers bowing.

dialogue.text: By around 1761, Mysore’s finances, forts and armies answered more to Hyder’s word than to the king’s seal. Yet the lion throne was left untouched, its occupant still the Wodeyar prince.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1761 तक मैसूर की दौलत, क़िले और फ़ौजें बादशाही मुहर से ज़्यादा हायदर के हुक्म पर चलती थीं। फिर भी शेर सिंहासन को हाथ न लगा, उस पर अब भी वोडेयार शहज़ादा ही बैठा रहा।

panels.shot: close-up profile of Hyder, distant out-of-focus king in background
panels.action: Hyder Ali’s face fills the foreground, calm and unreadable; beyond him, slightly blurred, Krishnaraja Wodeyar II sits under a canopy as priests conclude a ritual, incense smoke curling between them.

dialogue.text: Hyder knew the Wodeyars carried a century of royal memory. Their rituals, their lion emblem, their very presence turned his de facto rule into something that looked, and felt, acceptable to subjects and neighbors.

i18n.hi: हायदर जानता था कि वोडेयारों में सौ बरस की शाही यादें बसती हैं। उनके रिवाज़, शेर का निशान, और सिर्फ उनकी मौजूदगी ही उसके असली राज को रियाया और पड़ोसियों की नज़र में ऊपरी तौर पर क़ाबिले-क़बूल बना देती थी।

panels.shot: map-table top shot, hands of Hyder and emissaries pointing at Carnatic and Kolar
panels.action: Over a parchment map, Hyder Ali’s finger traces towards the Carnatic and Kolar while emissaries from coastal powers look on, their different turbans and coats showing French and Company styles.

dialogue.text: From this shadowed court, Hyder pushed outward—into the Carnatic, towards Kolar, towards weak points in the Maratha and Company spheres—testing alliances, buying time, and clipping enemies where he could.

i18n.hi: इसी छायादार दरबार से हायदर ने बाहर की तरफ धक्का दिया—कर्नाटक में, कोलार की दिशा में, मराठों और कंपनी की हल्की कड़ियों पर—सांठ-गांठ परखते, वक़्त ख़रीदते, और जहाँ बन पड़े दुश्मनों की पर काटते।

panels.shot: wide battle shot facing a mixed enemy line, with rockets streaking overhead
panels.action: On another campaign field, a combined enemy line of sepoys and allied horse braces as Mysore rockets streak in blazing arcs overhead, while Hyder Ali, banner behind him, sits firm in the saddle giving a sharp signal.

dialogue.text: The Company’s own secret reports would later note his stubborn, resourceful resistance—the iron rockets, the swift marches, the way his forces could appear, vanish and regroup before slower foes understood the pattern.

i18n.hi: कंपनी की गोपनीय रपटें बाद में उसके ज़िद्दी, सूझबूझ वाले मुक़ाबले को दर्ज करेंगी—लोहे के रॉकेट, तेज़ रफ़्तार कूच, और वो अंदाज़ कि उसकी फ़ौजें दिखें, ग़ायब हों, फिर कहीं और सँभल जाएँ, इससे पहले कि सुस्त दुश्मन कोई ढर्रा समझ पाएँ।

panels.shot: interior audience hall, British and Maratha envoys glimpsed at the edges, king central, Hyder slightly aside
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar II presides over a formal audience as Maratha and Company envoys stand at the hall’s edge; Hyder Ali sits on a lower seat to the side, listening keenly, his eyes weighing every word.

dialogue.text: To outside powers, protocol was clear. They bowed to the Wodeyar king, exchanged letters with the palace. Yet they knew that when decisions hardened into campaigns or treaties, Hyder’s consent was the one that mattered.

i18n.hi: बाहरी ताक़तों के लिए उसूल साफ़ था—वे वोडेयार राजा को सलाम करते, महल से ख़तों का लेन-देन होता। मगर सब जानते थे कि जब बातें सख़्त होकर जंग या समझौतों में ढलतीं, तो हायदर की रज़ामंदी ही असली तौल थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hyder issuing orders to officers in a more militarized administrative setting
panels.action: In a stark hall with ledgers stacked beside muskets and spears, Hyder Ali stands as officers and scribes listen; one wall bears muskets in neat racks, another shelf holds bound account books.

dialogue.speaker: Hyder Ali
dialogue.text: A state needs grain, coin, and guns in order. Bring me all three.

i18n.hi: “रियासत को अनाज, रुपया और बंदूकें सही हाल में चाहिए। ये तीनों मेरे पास पहुँचाओ।”

panels.shot: somber interior shot of Krishnaraja in a shrine, Hyder passing outside the doorway
panels.action: Within a small palace shrine, Krishnaraja Wodeyar II sits before a lamp-lit deity, eyes closed in prayer, while outside the open doorway Hyder Ali’s silhouette passes, brisk and purposeful, flanked by guards.

dialogue.text: The kingdom thus lived with two centers of gravity—ritual and lineage in the Wodeyar line, discipline and expansion in Hyder’s military state—entwined rather than openly colliding.

i18n.hi: यूँ रियासत दो गुरुत्व-केंद्रों के साथ जीती रही—रिवाज़ और वंश वोडेयारों में, और अनुशासन व फैलाव हायदर की फ़ौजी हुकूमत में—टकराव से ज़्यादा एक-दूसरे में लिपटे हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Srirangapatna fort and palace complex at dusk, lights glowing
panels.action: At dusk, the massive walls of Srirangapatna fort rise above the river, palace towers lit from within, watch fires burning along the ramparts as the sky darkens into indigo.

dialogue.text: From around 1761 until his death in 1782, Hyder Ali ruled effectively from this island fortress, while the Wodeyar king remained the visible sovereign—two faces of one Mysore in a contested Deccan.

i18n.hi: 1761 के आस-पास से 1782 में मौत तक, हायदर अली इसी टापू-क़िले से असल हुकूमत चलाता रहा, जबकि वोडेयार राजा सामने-सामने का बादशाह बना रहा—दक्खन की खींचतान में एक मैसूर के दो चेहरे।

panels.shot: close, reflective two-shot of both men older, seated apart in the same hall
panels.action: In a quieter moment years later, an older Krishnaraja Wodeyar II and an aging Hyder Ali sit at opposite ends of the same hall, each absorbed in thought, the space between them filled with banners, weapons and ritual objects.

dialogue.text: Their arrangement was not a communal conquest, but a hard-edged bargain of power and legitimacy—shaped by Maratha raids, Nizam intrigues and European companies hunting profit and ports.

i18n.hi: ये बंदोबस्त कोई कौमी फ़तह नहीं, बल्कि ताक़त और जायज़त का सख़्त सौदा था—जिसे मराठा धावों, निज़ाम की साज़िशों और बंदरगाह व मुनाफ़े के पीछे भागती यूरोपीय कंपनियों ने तराशा।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the empty lion throne and Hyder’s vacant chair beside it, lit by morning light
panels.action: The lion throne stands empty in the soft light of morning, a simpler chair beside it also vacant; beyond an open jali window the river glints, suggesting time’s flow and the passing of both men.

dialogue.text: When Hyder Ali died in 1782, and later when the Wodeyar line would again rise under British watch, Mysore’s story kept circling one lesson—that power can move without the crown itself ever seeming to shift.

i18n.hi: जब 1782 में हायदर अली मरा, और बाद में जब वोडेयार ख़ानदान फिर से अंग्रेज़ी निगरानी में उभरा, मैसूर की कहानी बार-बार एक सबक पर लौटती रही—कि ताक़त बदल सकती है, बिना ताज को हिलता हुआ दिखाए।

title_i18n.hi: छाया में सिंहासन थामे हायदर अली

subtitle_i18n.en: The General Who Ruled from Behind the Lion Throne
subtitle_i18n.hi: शेर सिंहासन के पीछे से हुकूमत करने वाला जनरल
